interpretations.rationale: Receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce (completed, exit 0, TestAssuranceRestoreCommittedLogsContext passed, 25 parsed events) closes the durability part of the question on a three-voter committed configuration. Reconstruction: comparison 0 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 22, where the restarted former leader held reconstructed_config_voters 1 while its own log's configuration entry at index 106 has three voters, and comparison 1 holds at parsed index 24, where the flag-disabled restart reconstructed three voters; the lost_inputs events at parsed indices 21 and 23 record the committed three-voter configuration at log index 106 against snapshot metadata carrying one voter. Durability: comparison 2 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 22, where the instance's Apply completed (acknowledged true, payload_index 113) yet the payload existed on exactly one copy of the committed configuration's members (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1, durable_on_majority false), the other two voters having reconstructed their own three-voter configuration, elected leadership among themselves and never received it; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 24, where the flag-disabled restart could not be a leader of the committed three-voter configuration with only itself running, so no commit was acknowledged at all ("node is not the leader") and nothing single-copy could be created. Mechanism: the reconstructed configurations.latest is what runFollower's eligibility branch, quorumSize for the candidacy and the leader commitment are computed from [follower_gate, candidate_quorum, quorum_size, leader_commitment, commitment_impl], and its divergence traces to the startup scan skipping the committed configuration entry [scan_start, restore_lastapplied]. Together with receipt faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1 (two-voter committed configuration: leadership with no election request and a completed commit while the other committed voter was stopped, comparisons holding at parsed indices 16, 17, 19 and 20) and receipt 63d4401225884bdd9c75fbe580336c63 (empty and stale reconstructions with reproducible bounded non-progress), the account is that RestoreCommittedLogs restarts can reconstruct a support basis the committed configuration does not sanction, bounded below by non-progress and above by client-acknowledged decisions resting on a minority of the committed configuration. Countervailing detail specific to this receipt: the acknowledged copy was not discarded during the observation, it stayed on the holder at index 113 after the holder rejoined, and the new leadership was elected in the same term as the stale leader (both 3), so what is established is a single-copy acknowledgement, not an erased entry; losing the acknowledged decision would additionally require the holder's own state to be lost, which this harness cannot express. The repair question stays open and is answered only from source so far: the other two voters never received the entry through ordinary replication while the holder's configuration stayed reconstructed [append_new].
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces the divergence and the non-progress: excluded by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same decisions.

The acknowledged payload survived on its holder in this receipt (payload_on_holder_after_rejoin true at index 113) and the new leadership formed in the same term, so no entry was erased; the consequence is that the acknowledgement was never durable on a majority, not that the entry is shown to be gone.
limitations: Single process with in-memory stores; the durability failure is shown as an absent majority copy, not as an unrecoverable loss of the holder's state.

investigations.question: When a node restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store, is the configuration it afterwards uses for elections and for counting committed support the committed configuration recorded in its own log, and what do a divergent reconstruction and the resulting support context do to decisions and progress?
investigations.hypothesis: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration only from configuration-carrying log entries above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); because restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the store's tracked commit index before that scan, a committed configuration entry at or below that index is never re-derived, so the restarted node keeps the configuration installed from snapshot metadata (or none at all when no snapshot exists) and then judges its own eligibility and support against that stale context.
investigations.discriminator: Whether an acknowledged commit that rested on a minority of the committed configuration is actually lost once a majority of the committed configuration that never held the entry forms new leadership (needs a committed configuration of three or more voters, where the reconstructed configuration is smaller), and whether any enabled path repairs a stale reconstruction without a later membership change.

gaps.question: Does any enabled path repair a restarted node's stale or empty configuration without a later membership change, for example ordinary AppendEntries from a healthy leader that still holds the entries?

Construction-time local feedback in this workspace (four cases: 1-voter and 2-voter bootstrapped clusters, 100 committed commands, 3000 ms observation window, in-memory transport and in-memory commit-tracking store) matched that account and is not a receipt: with the flag disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index equalled the configuration entry index persisted in its own log (1 and 103) and it reached Leader promptly in both shapes; with the flag enabled the same restarts produced a latest configuration index of 0 with an empty server set and no election attempt for the whole window (state Follower) in the no-snapshot shape, and a latest configuration index of 1 whose server set equalled the snapshot metadata's two-voter configuration (still containing the peer removed at log index 103, which the node skipped) in the snapshot-then-remove shape, where it stayed Candidate with about forty pre-vote campaigns and no leader. The earlier directions reproduce in the same run: comparison 6 is violated at parsed index 4 (no snapshot: no servers against the single-voter entry at index 1) and comparison 7 at parsed index 10 (snapshot-then-remove: the snapshot's two voters against the single-voter entry at index 103). Support consequences: comparison 2 holds at parsed index 17, where the flag-enabled instance became Leader (state_after_wait Leader, became_leader true) with election_requests 0, so it acquired authority without asking any member for a vote even though its own log's committed configuration has two voters; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 20, where the flag-disabled control tried to gather support (39 election requests) and stayed Candidate; comparison 5 holds at parsed index 20 with apply_ok false ("node is not the leader"), while comparison 4 holds at parsed index 17 with apply_ok true, so the commit completed with the other member of the committed two-voter configuration stopped and therefore without any second copy. Together these show a leadership decision and an acknowledged commit resting on support from one of the two committed voters, which the committed configuration does not permit: quorumSize and the leader commitment were computed from the reconstructed smaller configuration [candidate_quorum, quorum_size, leader_commitment, commitment_impl], and the reconstruction is the startup scan skipping the committed configuration entry [scan_start, restore_lastapplied]. Superseded: the earlier interpretation's open safety direction is now exercised for a two-voter committed configuration and moved from source-only to observed; its measurements for the other shapes are independently reproduced by this receipt at parsed indices 4 and 10. Still open: the acknowledged entry's fate when a majority of the committed configuration that never held it forms new leadership, which needs a committed configuration of three or more voters and is captured as the current discriminator; and the repair question, which remains answered only from source.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces the divergence and the non-progress: excluded in the previous receipt by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix (comparisons holding there with the flag enabled), and this receipt's flag-disabled controls hold the same configurations and refuse the same decisions.

Limits of the exercised consequence: the new shape stops every instance before the restart, so the stale leader is not contested by a live majority and the receipt establishes which support the decisions rested on, not an observed competing leader or an observed lost entry.
limitations: The bounded observations use one process with in-memory stores and a 3000 ms leadership window plus a 1000 ms commit timeout; they are not an unbounded liveness or durability proof.

The lost-decision consequence is not exercised: with a committed configuration of exactly two voters no other majority can elect without the entry, so an acknowledged entry that rests on one copy cannot yet be shown to be discarded.
Not exercised: disk-backed commit-tracking stores, crashes during the restart, restarted peers rejoining after the acknowledged commit, and post-restart membership changes or snapshot installs.
Only the demote/snapshot/promote ladder and the remove-after-snapshot shapes were exercised; skip windows produced by longer committed sequences were not varied.

result.summary: Recorded the current account for the lost-commit receipt c7938884cd87410eb02432e32dc092ce (25 events, exit 0): comparison 0 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 22 (the restarted former leader held one reconstructed voter against the three-voter entry at log index 106; control holds at 24) and comparison 2 is violated at the same index — its Apply completed (acknowledged, payload index 113) while the payload existed on exactly one of the three committed voters (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1), the other two having reconstructed their own three-voter configuration and elected leadership without ever receiving it; the flag-disabled control acknowledged nothing at all (index 24). So a client-acknowledged decision rested on a minority of the committed configuration. Added a durability fact for that, extended the reconstruction fact to the three-voter ladder, kept the repair gap open and moved the discriminator to the unexecuted live-cluster repair question. Counterevidence recorded explicitly: the acknowledged copy was not discarded in the window (it stayed on the holder at index 113) and the new leadership formed in the same term as the stale leader, so the established failure is a single-copy acknowledgement, not an erased entry. Incomplete: the follower-repair probe (a restarted follower that stays in a cluster with a healthy leader) is not built yet.

investigations.question: When a node restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store, is the configuration it afterwards uses for elections and for counting committed support the committed configuration recorded in its own log, and what do a divergent reconstruction and the resulting support context do to decisions and progress?
investigations.hypothesis: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration only from configuration-carrying log entries above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); because restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the store's tracked commit index before that scan, a committed configuration entry at or below that index is never re-derived, so the restarted node keeps the configuration installed from snapshot metadata (or none at all when no snapshot exists) and then judges its own eligibility and support against that stale context.
investigations.discriminator: Whether a healthy leader's ordinary replication repairs the stale reconstruction of a restarted follower that stays in the cluster (its log already matching the leader's), and whether a later configuration entry appended by that leader does repair it.

gaps.question: Does any enabled path repair a restarted node's stale or empty configuration without a later membership change, for example ordinary AppendEntries from a healthy leader that still holds the entries?

knowledge.statement: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration from configuration-carrying log entries only for indices above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); the other writers of r.configurations are snapshot restore, snapshot install and the leader's own appendConfigurationEntry path, and nothing else repairs it.
knowledge.conditions: Startup reconstruction in NewRaft over a log store; lastApplied may already be advanced by restoreFromCommittedLogs or by a restored snapshot; configuration entries are identified by LogConfiguration or the deprecated peer entry types.

knowledge.statement: restoreFromCommittedLogs reads the commit index from a CommitTrackingLogStore, clamps it to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs, which applies the committed prefix to the FSM and sets lastApplied to that commit index; this happens after snapshot restore and before NewRaft's configuration scan.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the tracked commit index is at least the index of a configuration entry stored in the log.

knowledge.statement: The configuration a node holds decides its own participation and support arithmetic: runFollower declines to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote in the latest configuration, a candidate needs quorumSize() votes of the latest configuration, and the leader's commitment is constructed from the latest configuration, so a stale or empty reconstruction directly changes which support is required and counted.
knowledge.conditions: The configuration is the one reconstructed at startup or later written by a snapshot install or a configuration change; quorumSize and the commitment are computed from configurations.latest.

knowledge.statement: appendEntries processes configuration entries only for the entries it newly appends; entries already present at the same index and term are skipped, so ordinary replication from a healthy leader does not re-derive the configuration of a follower whose log already matches.
knowledge.conditions: Follower handling a normal AppendEntries whose entries are duplicates of its own log; entries that are in the leader's compacted prefix instead arrive as an InstallSnapshot, which rewrites both configurations from the snapshot metadata.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across three ladders: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; and the three-voter ladder reported one voter against the three-voter entry at log index 106. The public GetConfiguration view reported the same value, and the flag-disabled controls and the within-flag case whose configuration entry sits above the replayed prefix all reconstructed the entry's own index and voter count.
knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); no membership change is issued after the restart.

interpretations.rationale: Source-based account, no retained receipt yet. NewRaft re-derives the node's own configuration only from configuration-carrying log entries above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied) [scan_start], and with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs over a CommitTrackingLogStore the preceding restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the store's tracked commit index [restore_lastapplied, restore_doc], so a committed configuration entry at or below that index is never re-derived and r.configurations keeps whatever restoreSnapshot installed from snapshot metadata [snapshot_cfg] (nothing at all when no snapshot exists). That reconstructed context is what the node then uses: runFollower refuses to campaign when latestIndex is zero or the local ID has no vote [follower_gate], votesNeeded is quorumSize() of the latest configuration [candidate_quorum], and the leader commitment is built from the latest configuration [leader_commitment]. Duplicate entries in an AppendEntries are skipped without reprocessing their configuration entries [append_new], so ordinary replication from a healthy leader does not repair the reconstruction; only a newly appended configuration entry, an installed snapshot, or a restart with the flag disabled rewrites it [install_snapshot_cfg, cfg_entry]. Construction-time local feedback in this workspace (four cases: 1-voter and 2-voter bootstrapped clusters, 100 committed commands, 3000 ms observation window, in-memory transport and in-memory commit-tracking store) matched that account and is not a receipt: with the flag disabled the restarted voter's latest configuration index equalled the configuration entry index persisted in its own log (1 and 103) and it reached Leader promptly in both shapes; with the flag enabled the same restarts produced a latest configuration index of 0 with an empty server set and no election attempt for the whole window (state Follower) in the no-snapshot shape, and a latest configuration index of 1 whose server set equalled the snapshot metadata's two-voter configuration (still containing the peer removed at log index 103, which the node skipped) in the snapshot-then-remove shape, where it stayed Candidate with about forty pre-vote campaigns and no leader. The requested execution compares those observations against the persisted configuration entry under a disabled-flag control; until its receipt exists the conclusion and any defect judgment remain unresolved.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.
limitations: No retained execution exists yet: the account rests on source inspection plus construction-time local feedback, not on a receipt.
Not exercised: disk-backed commit-tracking stores, crashes during the restart, and any later client membership change or snapshot install that could rewrite the configuration.
The bounded progress observation is a 3000 ms window (60 x ElectionTimeout of 50 ms) over one process; it is not an unbounded liveness proof.

Source-supported but unexecuted: when the skipped committed entries add voters, the reconstructed configuration has fewer voters than the committed one, so quorumSize() and the leader commitment can treat support that is not a majority of the committed configuration as sufficient; that safety direction is not exercised by this probe.

Only two committed shapes (a single bootstrap voter, and a single voter left by a committed RemoveServer) were exercised; the exercised consequence is bounded non-progress and a wrong support basis, not an observed lost decision.

The earlier directions reproduce in the same run: comparison 6 is violated at parsed index 4 (no snapshot: no servers against the single-voter entry at index 1) and comparison 7 at parsed index 10 (snapshot-then-remove: the snapshot's two voters against the single-voter entry at index 103). Support consequences: comparison 2 holds at parsed index 17, where the flag-enabled instance became Leader (state_after_wait Leader, became_leader true) with election_requests 0, so it acquired authority without asking any member for a vote even though its own log's committed configuration has two voters; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 20, where the flag-disabled control tried to gather support (39 election requests) and stayed Candidate; comparison 5 holds at parsed index 20 with apply_ok false ("node is not the leader"), while comparison 4 holds at parsed index 17 with apply_ok true, so the commit completed with the other member of the committed two-voter configuration stopped and therefore without any second copy. Superseded: the earlier interpretation's open safety direction is now exercised for a two-voter committed configuration and moved from source-only to observed; its measurements for the other shapes are independently reproduced by this receipt at parsed indices 4 and 10. Still open: the acknowledged entry's fate when a majority of the committed configuration that never held it forms new leadership, which needs a committed configuration of three or more voters and is captured as the current discriminator; and the repair question, which remains answered only from source.
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Limits of the exercised consequence: the new shape stops every instance before the restart, so the stale leader is not contested by a live majority and the receipt establishes which support the decisions rested on, not an observed competing leader or an observed lost entry.
limitations: The bounded observations use one process with in-memory stores and a 3000 ms leadership window plus a 1000 ms commit timeout; they are not an unbounded liveness or durability proof.

The lost-decision consequence is not exercised: with a committed configuration of exactly two voters no other majority can elect without the entry, so an acknowledged entry that rests on one copy cannot yet be shown to be discarded.

Durability: comparison 2 is violated with a valid witness at parsed index 22, where the instance's Apply completed (acknowledged true, payload_index 113) yet the payload existed on exactly one copy of the committed configuration's members (payload_on_victims 0, durable_copies 1, durable_on_majority false), the other two voters having reconstructed their own three-voter configuration, elected leadership among themselves and never received it; comparison 3 holds at parsed index 24, where the flag-disabled restart could not be a leader of the committed three-voter configuration with only itself running, so no commit was acknowledged at all ("node is not the leader") and nothing single-copy could be created. Mechanism: the reconstructed configurations.latest is what runFollower's eligibility branch, quorumSize for the candidacy and the leader commitment are computed from [follower_gate, candidate_quorum, quorum_size, leader_commitment, commitment_impl], and its divergence traces to the startup scan skipping the committed configuration entry [scan_start, restore_lastapplied]. Together with receipt faa52ef8ac8a422aa26e12582959eda1 (two-voter committed configuration: leadership with no election request and a completed commit while the other committed voter was stopped, comparisons holding at parsed indices 16, 17, 19 and 20) and receipt 63d4401225884bdd9c75fbe580336c63 (empty and stale reconstructions with reproducible bounded non-progress), the account is that RestoreCommittedLogs restarts can reconstruct a support basis the committed configuration does not sanction, bounded below by non-progress and above by client-acknowledged decisions resting on a minority of the committed configuration. Countervailing detail specific to this receipt: the acknowledged copy was not discarded during the observation, it stayed on the holder at index 113 after the holder rejoined, and the new leadership was elected in the same term as the stale leader (both 3), so what is established is a single-copy acknowledgement, not an erased entry; losing the acknowledged decision would additionally require the holder's own state to be lost, which this harness cannot express. The repair question stays open and is answered only from source so far: the other two voters never received the entry through ordinary replication while the holder's configuration stayed reconstructed [append_new].
counterevidence: The feature's documented purpose is replaying known-committed logs into the FSM; nothing in the sources makes skipping committed configuration entries a required behaviour, and the existing TestRaft_RestoreCommittedLogs asserts only applied index, tracked commit index and log indices, so it neither exercises nor contradicts the configuration reconstruction.

Competing explanation that the flag's committed-log replay itself, rather than the skipped configuration entry, produces the divergence and the non-progress: excluded by the within-flag case whose configuration entry lies above the replayed prefix and by the flag-disabled controls in every receipt, which hold the published configuration and refuse the same decisions.

The acknowledged payload survived on its holder in this receipt (payload_on_holder_after_rejoin true at index 113) and the new leadership formed in the same term, so no entry was erased; the consequence is that the acknowledgement was never durable on a majority, not that the entry is shown to be gone.
limitations: Single process with in-memory stores; the durability failure is shown as an absent majority copy, not as an unrecoverable loss of the holder's state.

The two voters brought back after the acknowledged commit were deliberately restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs disabled so that their own configuration comes from their logs; their leadership therefore exercises the correct configuration, which is what makes the payload's absence observable.
The acknowledged commit is a single payload acknowledged in one leadership window; no rate, repetition or longer-sequence claim follows.
The repair question remains unexecuted, and disk-backed stores, crashes during the restart and post-restart membership changes are still not exercised.
